rules: Every accepted row names the exact command, cwd, platform, runtime, fixture and operation, expected and actual result, evidence level and structured artifacts with role, path, byte size and sha256.

A row may only claim the evidence class its own operation evidence can reach: source inspection, fixture generation, a model and a contract harness never satisfy a browser, real-adapter or product-E2E requirement.
Evidence levels are separated: source-read, fixture-generation, modeled, harness, engine-round-trip, browser-real, product-e2e.
Missing rows stay pending with a reason so the register remains valid while the go/no-go decision stays NO-GO.
A declared PASS without structured artifact, operation and assertion evidence is invalid, not merely unproven.
G0 requires the six format cycles and the DOC-004 fault-case and DOC-005 mandatory-case gates; it does not require the G3 advanced port or the G7 product E2E.

Each required core-cycle gate needs an accepted row run in the Orca embedded browser (Chromium) on Windows, recording both the Orca application version and the embedded Chromium version: the G0 browser decision of 2026-09-25. Installed Windows Chrome/Edge and macOS/Safari rows are not required at G0 and never satisfy a required G0 gate (see browserDeferrals); the existing accepted scoped Chrome/Edge/Chromium rows stay valid as non-gate evidence.
Row format, row kind and operation id are bound to the gate: a retargeted row does not satisfy it and the verifier reports the mismatch as an error.
Every required assertion and every required fault or mandatory case needs its own accepted row; a bundle PASS must not hide a missing or failed case.

A core-cycle row binds its own fixture, format and operation: every artifact ref must equal fixture/format/operationId, and an immutable input, the persisted output, a report/transcript and independent render/extraction evidence are separate artifact identities. One artifact file belongs to one accepted row (identified by its resolved path, not its spelling), so two browsers or two formats cannot attest one set of files. Identical bytes in two distinct files remain valid: two deterministic runs may publish the same content.

DOC-005 keeps two honest halves on one contract gate. Draft-persistence cases need a real local-store persisted-output artifact plus a fresh-store recovery assertion; authorization-only cases must declare authMode "modeled" and may not claim a real adapter. G0 never claims a real product authorization backend.

A coverage shortfall (a missing assertion, case, artifact or browser) is a warning that keeps the register valid and the gate unsatisfied; a contradiction (a retargeted row, a weakened floor, a tampered or shared artifact identity, an unlabeled auth claim) is an error.
Q1-B stays a pilot requirement tracked in registry.q1b and registry.pilot; it is reported separately and never gates the G0 decision.

A required core row binds ONE primary manifest fixture (fixture) which must be able to meet every required assertion; fixtureRebinds records a row moved off a fixture that cannot, and the retired fixture may stay as that row's supportingFixture. A row whose primary fixture is the retired side of a rebind for its format is reported and cannot satisfy the gate.

A required core-cycle row must name a fixture id that exists in docs/office/g0/fixtures/manifest.json (the verifier reads it and reports unknown-fixture-id as an error); a supportingFixture and both sides of a fixtureRebinds entry are checked the same way.

The labs self-stop on their max-hold; the original 1h v2 lab run expired at 05:46Z and the PDF lab was restarted on ports 5624-5627 for the independent Tester round (the Tester earlier reached the expired-lab error page, recorded as an environment failure, not a candidate failure).

The patch is lab-only and candidate: it implements the two missing pdfApi render capabilities of the image-edit flow with the real pdfjs 6.2.108 + @napi-rs/canvas 1.0.3 path (no stub bytes), is anchor-based so the whole-file sha256 is provenance and not a write gate: it composes with a core-docx-pptx lab-server hunk in either order, refuses by name when its own anchors are missing or ambiguous or when the block is already present, and writes nothing on a refusal (proved through the real CLI, not only the library). Tests: S/lab-patch/pageImagePng.test.mjs 12/12 + pageImagePng-compose.test.mjs 11/11 = 23/23 on the pinned Node 22, including the revision C base (rev-C postimage f01b57de2eb8ef5bfc976a5af4814873eeaa686976db0433d57a7715d6600b99) and the no-stacking re-apply regression.

Two real defects in the slice PDF oracle were found by running it on the engine output and fixed without weakening any assertion: (a) the SMask branch returned an object where a Buffer was required, so an alpha image (the cutout output) crashed the decoder - the mask alpha is now applied to the image RGBA; (b) image-changed required the same XObject name, which would fail the engine real replacement shape - the oracle now also accepts a new object with different decoded pixels while the page keeps its image count. Regression tests: tools/oracle-pdf.test.mjs 12/12 plus tools/oracle-pdf-replacement.test.mjs 2/2 (the negative case new-object-identical-pixels still fails).
The marker text was typed with the Orca type command after Ctrl+A, never filled; no IME or Vietnamese composition path was exercised.

The lab runner and engine hosts ran on Node 25.8.0 (holder process) and the tools on Node 22.23.2; Orca embedded browser only (G0 decision g115): no installed Chrome/Edge, no macOS/Safari, no full PDF product or pilot claim.

FE review r1 finding F1 (excludeAnnots): the lab render module now accepts the renderer excludeAnnots field and erases those rects exactly like excludeRects (unit tests: 12/12 including a pixel-level erase proof and the byte-identical excludeRects comparison; live probe on the restarted lab: excludeAnnots returned the same 849-byte raster as the equivalent excludeRects call, and 855 bytes without any exclusion - receipts/lead/lab/pagePreviewPng-excludeAnnots-probe.json). The additive build r7-pdf-pageimage2 bundles the frozen adapter revision 1b6db9c5, which does not forward excludeAnnots, so the end-to-end annotation-delete erase path is not exercised by this cycle and is recorded as an open lab-only gap: the row cycle has no annotation deletes, and a v3 additive build would be needed to exercise that combination end to end.

Tooling defect found and fixed during the F1 re-apply: the first version of the anchor-based re-apply computed the postimage from whatever the replica already carried, so a forced re-apply stacked a second insertion (observed as lab-server 5fbf2c4b -> 973b241f -> c9d6248a). The transform base is now the pinned preimage whenever the replica already carries this patch, the composed path is the only in-place transform, the replica was restored from the pinned preimage and re-applied cleanly, and a regression test asserts that a second --force-reapply run changes neither file and reports unchanged-postimage for all three.
